title: From Voice AI Demo to Production: Why Infrastructure and Agent Supervision Matter
summary: Explore Twilio’s new Voice AI infrastructure features from Conversation Relay, Agent Connect, and Conversation Intelligence.
body_markdown:
Every week, another company announces an AI voice agent. Most announcements focus on the model: how smart it is, how natural it sounds, or how quickly it can respond.


But the real test starts when that AI agent takes a live customer call.


Real conversations are not controlled demos. Customers pause mid-thought, interrupt, switch languages, call from noisy environments, or need a human handoff. Speech providers can experience latency. Calls can degrade. And once an AI agent is live, teams need to know what it actually said, whether it completed the task, and where the experience needs improvement.


That gap between a compelling demo and a trusted production deployment is where Voice AI succeeds or fails.


Today, we are expanding our Voice AI infrastructure with new capabilities across[Conversation Relay](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/conversational-ai/conversationrelay) ,[Twilio Agent Connect](https://www.twilio.com/docs/conversations/agent-connect) , and[Conversation Intelligence](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/products/conversational-ai/conversational-intelligence) to help your teams build, scale, and supervise AI-powered conversations in production.


Together, these enhancements help you solve three challenges that are often treated separately:


- Make AI agents work reliably in real-time voice conversations
- Give your teams flexibility to use the models, speech providers, and agent frameworks you choose
- Help you supervise agent quality and improve performance at scale


Twilio is not trying to be your AI agent or your model. We provide the communications infrastructure and quality visibility that help make any AI agent production-ready.


## A great model is not a production Voice AI strategy


A strong model is only one part of the Voice AI experience. In production, customer trust is shaped by everything around the model: whether your agent interrupts, whether the call stays connected, whether the audio is clear, and whether the experience can adapt as the conversation changes.


That is why we’re adding[new Conversation Relay capabilities](https://www.twilio.com/docs/voice/conversationrelay) designed for real-world voice interactions.


### Smart Turn Detection (GA)


Your AI agent needs to know the difference between a customer finishing a thought and simply pausing to think.


Smart Turn Detection helps agents better identify when someone is actually done speaking, reducing awkward interruptions, premature responses, and dead air.


### Automated STT Failover (GA)


In a live call, a speech provider issue can quickly turn into a poor customer experience.


**Automated STT Failover** helps preserve call continuity by routing to a backup speech-to-text provider when the primary provider experiences latency, rate limits, or stream disruptions, without requiring your team to build custom failover logic.


### Dynamic Configuration Parameters (GA)


Conversations change in real time. A caller may switch languages, introduce specialized terminology, or move into a different workflow.


**Dynamic Configuration Parameters** let your team update speech hints, languages, and voice settings mid-call without restarting or disrupting the conversation.


### HD Audio (GA)


Clearer audio gives AI systems better input.


**HD Audio** provides higher-fidelity voice input to support stronger speech recognition, better understanding, and fewer “can you repeat that?” moments.


### Advanced Conversational Voice (GA)


Natural conversations require more than accurate words. They require tone, pacing, and clarity.


With support for advanced conversational voice models like **ElevenLabs v4 Turbo** , your teams can deliver more expressive, natural AI voice experiences across 90+ languages.


## Reliability should not require locking into one AI vendor


Many Voice AI platforms require you to adopt a single model, framework, or vendor roadmap. That may work in the short term, but the AI landscape is changing quickly. The model or provider that performs best today may not be the best fit twelve months from now.


Your production infrastructure should not force that bet.


[Twilio Agent Connect](https://www.twilio.com/docs/conversations/agent-connect) helps your teams connect external AI agent frameworks and LLM runtimes to Twilio voice and messaging channels. That means you can bring the AI stack you already use, whether that includes[AWS,](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/integrations/ai-twilio-agent-connect-amazon-bedrock-agentcore)[Google Cloud](https://github.com/twilio/twilio-agent-connect-google) ,[Microsoft Azure](https://www.twilio.com/docs/conversations/agent-connect/integrations/microsoft-foundry) ,[OpenAI’s speech-to-speech models](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/developers/tutorials/integrations/tac-gpt-live-voice-ai-agent-typescript) , or your own custom agent runtime, while relying on Twilio for the communications layer underneath.


The value is giving your teams flexibility across your AI stack — and a faster path from prototype to production.


You can continue investing in the agent experiences, prompts, tools, workflows, and business logic that differentiate your product, while Twilio helps handle the communications infrastructure required to reach customers across channels.


## Deploying an agent is the easy part, knowing what it says is the hard part


As AI agents handle more customer interactions, they are becoming a new front door to your business. They answer questions, complete tasks, and act on behalf of your company.


That makes supervision critical. You need to know what your agents are saying, whether they are completing tasks, when customers need help, and where the experience needs to improve.


Traditional LLM observability tools show internal model activity, but they do not always reveal what was actually said over the customer communication channel. Twilio


Conversation Intelligence provides a transcript-first view of AI and human interactions, helping your teams evaluate real customer conversations without changing agent code or installing intrusive SDKs.


We are expanding[Conversation Intelligence](https://www.twilio.com/docs/conversations/intelligence) with new capabilities designed to make AI agent supervision easier to operationalize at scale:


- **Twilio-authored operators (Public Beta)** Prebuilt operators that analyze AI agent transcripts for key quality signals, including task completion and hallucination detection.[See our most recent Twilio-authored operators.](https://www.twilio.com/en-us/blog/products/launches/conversation-intelligence-operators-ai-agent-supervision)
- **Conversation Intelligence On-Demand Execution API** **(GA)** Gives teams the flexibility to run Language Operators on demand alongside automated triggers, so they can analyze conversations when and how their workflows require.


Together, these capabilities help your teams monitor AI agent performance, evaluate conversation quality, and identify issues across large volumes of customer interactions without being locked into a single agent platform or model provider.


They also lay the groundwork for a broader supervision layer for agentic customer engagement, where your business can define the performance signals that matter most, analyze conversations at scale, and continuously improve how AI and human agents serve your customers.


## Built for continuous Voice AI innovation


The Voice AI market is crowded with companies building agents. But production Voice AI requires more than an agent. It requires infrastructure that can handle live conversations, preserve flexibility across a fast-changing AI ecosystem, and give you visibility into what your agents are actually doing.


That is where Twilio is focused.


With Conversation Relay, Agent Connect, and Conversation Intelligence, Twilio helps your teams:


- Connect AI agents to real customer conversations
- Use the models, speech providers, and cloud runtimes you choose
- Improve reliability, audio quality, and conversational flow
- Supervise agent behavior and conversation quality at scale
- Continuously improve AI-powered customer experiences


This release is part of Twilio’s ongoing investment in Voice AI infrastructure, helping your business move beyond demos and build AI agents your customers can trust in production.


## Start building production-ready Voice AI with Twilio


Your teams should be able to keep control of your AI strategy, including your models, agents, prompts, tools, and business logic, while relying on Twilio for the communications infrastructure and quality visibility required to operate AI-powered conversations in production.
